title: VOID PVP — Rust/Java WS protocol
description: Every message on the localhost WebSocket between the Rust launcher (server, `void-bridge`) and the Java mod (client, `net/`), as specified in PVP_ARCHITECTURE.md §7. One JSON object per WS text frame, discriminated on `t`. The link carries state and telemetry summaries only, never per-frame data (§2): telemetry that is drawn never leaves the JVM. Forward compatibility rule of §7: a receiver ignores an unknown `t` and ignores unknown fields, which is why every message here sets additionalProperties true. `v` is the protocol version and is carried only on the two handshake messages, `hello` and `init`; a mismatch makes the launcher refuse to launch and prompt for an update, since mod and launcher ship together. Connection parameters reach the JVM as -Dvoid.port and -Dvoid.token (§6.9).

oneOf.description: A message sent by the mod to the launcher.
A message sent by the launcher to the mod.

protocol_version.title: Protocol version
protocol_version.description: Version of this message set. Bumped on any breaking change. Carried on `hello` and `init` only; both sides compare and refuse to proceed on a mismatch (§7). **2** since `init.loadouts` changed from `loadout_summary` to whole loadouts: a v1 mod would read a v2 `init` without complaint, but a v2 mod against a v1 launcher would receive summaries, materialise every mod at its factory default, and silently apply the wrong loadout on a switch. That is exactly the mixed-halves case `v` exists to refuse.

java_to_rust.description: The thirteen messages the mod sends to the launcher. Validate an inbound frame in `void-bridge` against this.

rust_to_java.title: Rust to Java
rust_to_java.description: The six messages the launcher sends to the mod. Validate an inbound frame in the mod's `net/` package against this.

oneOf.description: Handshake reply carrying the initial world of state.
Loadout switched from the launcher or the tray.
Global settings changed in the launcher.
Equipped cosmetics: the local player's own set and other VOID players' sets.
Another VOID player on the same server played an emote.
The loadout library changed in the launcher, or Rust refused an in-game change to it.

msg_hello.title: hello (Java to Rust)
msg_hello.description: First frame the mod sends after the WS connects. Identifies the game and mod build and authenticates with the session token the launcher passed as -Dvoid.token. The launcher answers with `init`.

mc.description: Minecraft version the mod is running inside, e.g. `1.8.9`.

mod.description: Semantic version of the void-client mod build.

token.description: Session token the launcher generated for this spawn and passed as -Dvoid.token. The launcher rejects and closes the socket if it does not match.

msg_state.title: state (Java to Rust)
msg_state.description: Sent by the mod on every change to live loadout state, as a flat patch of dotted paths (§7). Java is authoritative for live state (§6.1); this message tells Rust what already happened, it never asks for permission. Batched per change, not per frame.

loadout.description: Id of the loadout the patch applies to; the loadout that was active when the change was made.

patch.description: Changed fields as a flat map of dotted path to new value.

state_patch.title: State patch
state_patch.description: Flat map of dotted paths into the loadout to their new values, e.g. `{"mods.fullbright.on": true}`. Flat rather than nested so that concurrent changes to sibling settings merge without conflict. Paths address `mods.<mod_id>.<setting>` only; HUD layout changes travel in the `hud` message instead.

propertyNames.description: A dotted path of the form mods.<mod_id>.<setting>.

additionalProperties.description: The new value at that path. Type depends on the setting; validate against the mod's settings sub-schema in mods.json after applying.

msg_hud.title: hud (Java to Rust)
msg_hud.description: Sent by the mod when the HUD editor commits a drag (§9, Figma 244:1722). Carries the whole layout for the loadout rather than a delta, because the editor already holds the full list and a whole-list write cannot leave Rust with a partially moved layout.

loadout.description: Id of the loadout whose HUD layout this replaces.

items.description: The complete new HUD layout, replacing whatever Rust had stored for this loadout.

msg_globals.title: globals (Java to Rust)
msg_globals.description:
Sent by the mod when a global setting is written in game — the in-game Settings page rebinding the menu key, the HUD editor's Snap toggle writing `hud_editor_grid`. The exact counterpart of `state` for the non-loadout half of §8.3: Java is authoritative, has already applied the change, and this tells Rust so it reaches `settings.json` and survives the process. Without it a global written in game lives only in `LiveState` and is gone at the next launch, which is what `hud_editor_grid` did for as long as the Snap toggle existed.

A **delta, not the whole object**, and that is load-bearing rather than stylistic. `global_settings` is `additionalProperties: true` so the launcher may add a global without a protocol bump, but the mod's `GlobalSettings` is a fixed five-field class that cannot carry one — so a mod that echoed the whole object back would silently erase every global it does not model. Rust merges the named keys into what it already has and leaves the rest alone.

patch.description: The globals that changed, and only those.

global_patch.title: Global settings patch
global_patch.description: Flat map of `global_settings` property names to their new values, e.g. `{"hud_editor_grid": 8}`. Keys are the top-level property names of `global_settings`, not dotted paths: globals are flat, so there is nothing to path into. Unlike `state_patch` there is no `null`: `setGlobal` refuses a value it cannot store and returns null to the caller rather than sending one, so a null here would mean nothing a receiver could act on.

additionalProperties.description: The new value. Validate against the property's sub-schema in `global_settings` after applying; the mod has already clamped it to the same bounds.

msg_session.title: session (Java to Rust)
msg_session.description: Telemetry summary the mod sends every 60 seconds and once more on exit (§7). Feeds the played-time, average-fps and average-ping numbers on the launcher's Home (Last session). Values are cumulative for the current game session, not deltas.

fps_avg.description: Mean frames per second over the session so far.

played_ms.description: Milliseconds elapsed since the game window opened.

ping_avg.description: Mean of the player's own ping readings (`NetworkPlayerInfo.responseTime`) over the session so far, in milliseconds. Only readings taken on a server count, so it is absent until there has been one and singleplayer never sends it. Optional and additive: a launcher that predates it ignores it, as it does any unknown field.

server.description: Host of the server the player is on, or null in the main menu or singleplayer.

loadout.description: Id of the loadout active at the time of the report. Optional; Rust attributes stats to the loadout it last saw active when absent.

msg_server.title: server (Java to Rust)
msg_server.description: Sent by the mod on connect to and disconnect from a multiplayer server, mirroring the `server` bridge event. Lets the launcher show current presence and, later, server-bound default loadouts (open question §16.3).

host.description: Hostname of the server, without port, e.g. `mc.hypixel.net`. Empty string when disconnecting.

connected.description: True on connect, false on disconnect.

port.description: Port of the server when it is not the default 25565.

msg_hotkey.title: hotkey (Java to Rust)
msg_hotkey.description: Sent when the player pressed one of the two global hotkeys of §6.3 in game. It is a notification, not a request: Java has already done the thing — cycled the loadout, opened or closed the overlay — and this tells the launcher so the tray and the launcher window can follow. The loadout that the L key selected still travels in its own `state` message; this one carries no state of its own, which is why the payload is a single id.

msg_loadout_save.title: loadout_save (Java to Rust)
msg_loadout_save.description: Sent when the in-game Loadouts screen created, renamed, duplicated or imported a loadout, or changed its quick pins (`window.void` calls of the same names). Carries the whole loadout: Rust creates it at the end of the library order when the id is new and overwrites it otherwise, validating it first. Like `state`, a notification of what Java already did, not a request; if Rust cannot store it, it answers with `library` so the game shows what is actually on disk.

loadout.description: The loadout as Java now holds it.

msg_loadout_delete.title: loadout_delete (Java to Rust)
msg_loadout_delete.description: Sent when the in-game Loadouts screen deleted a loadout. Java has already removed it, and switched away from it first when it was active (that switch travels as its own `loadout_select`). Rust never deletes the last loadout on disk.

msg_loadout_select.title: loadout_select (Java to Rust)
msg_loadout_select.description: Sent when the player picked a loadout in game other than with the cycle key, which reports itself as `hotkey` `loadout.next`. Moves Rust's active pointer so the tray and the next launch agree with the running game.

msg_library.title: library (Rust to Java)
msg_library.description: The whole loadout library, in full and in library order, exactly as `init.loadouts`. Sent when the launcher created, deleted, imported or edited a loadout while the game is running, and as the answer to an in-game `loadout_save` or `loadout_delete` Rust could not apply. Java replaces its library with it, keeping its own live copy of the active loadout, and pushes the `loadouts` bridge event.

loadouts.description: Every loadout, in full and in library order.

hotkey_id.title: Hotkey id
hotkey_id.description: Closed set of the global hotkeys the mod reports. `loadout.next` is the L-key cycle of §6.3, already applied when this is sent. `overlay` is the menu key (Right Shift by default) opening or closing VoidMenuScreen; the launcher uses it only for presence, since the menu is entirely in-game.

msg_init.title: init (Rust to Java)
msg_init.description: The launcher's answer to `hello` (§6.9). Delivers the entire world of persisted state in one frame: the active loadout, **every other loadout in full**, and global settings. The mod keeps no config files of its own (§6.1); everything it knows arrives here. `loadouts` carries whole loadouts rather than summaries on purpose: a loadout is roughly 1 KB and a library is capped at 128, so the whole library is a few hundred kilobytes at worst, sent once per launch — and in exchange `void.switchLoadout` and the L-key cycle can apply any loadout in under a frame (§8.2) with no round trip, and the in-game Loadouts screen can list the library without a bridge accessor of its own. There is deliberately no `request_loadout` message: nothing the mod does needs one.

v.description: Protocol version the launcher speaks. The mod disconnects and reports a version mismatch if it differs from its own.

loadout.description: The full active loadout to apply immediately.

loadouts.description: Every loadout in the library, in full and in library order, including the active one. Backs the L-key cycle, the in-game switcher and the `loadouts` bridge event.

settings.description: Global, non-loadout settings that affect the game session.

msg_loadout.title: loadout (Rust to Java)
msg_loadout.description: Sent when the loadout was switched outside the game, from the launcher UI or the tray's Switch loadout submenu (§5, §8.2). Java applies it exactly as it applies an in-game switch, then pushes the `loadout` bridge event to the UI. Java does not answer with `state`; the launcher already knows.

loadout.description: The full loadout to switch to.

msg_settings.title: settings (Rust to Java)
msg_settings.description: Sent when global settings changed in the launcher while the game is running, e.g. the player rebound the menu key. Carries the whole settings object, not a delta.

msg_cosmetics_query.title: cosmetics_query (Java to Rust)
msg_cosmetics_query.description: The UUIDs of players the mod currently sees (tab list and rendered entities), whose cosmetics it wants. The mod batches, debounces and caches on its side; the launcher batch-fetches from the online backend (`cosmetics-lookup`) behind its own LRU cache and answers with one or more `cosmetics` messages. UUIDs that are not VOID players never appear in a reply: absence is the answer. The mod never talks HTTP; Rust owns network and auth (docs/online-contract.md).

uuids.description: Minecraft UUIDs, dashed or undashed. At most 200 per message; send more as several.

msg_emote_local.title: emote (Java to Rust)
msg_emote_local.description: The local player played an emote from their wheel. Java has already started the animation locally; the launcher relays it to the other VOID players on the same server through the online backend, which checks ownership and stamps the sender's identity. Same `t` as the launcher's `emote`; the direction tells them apart, and this one carries no `uuid`.

not.description: A `uuid` makes it the launcher's relay, `msg_emote_remote`.

msg_equip.title: equip (Java to Rust)
msg_equip.description: The player equipped an item, or took one off with `id: null`, in the in-game wardrobe (`window.void.equipCosmetic`). Java has already applied it locally; the launcher persists it to the online backend, which validates ownership. If the backend refuses (not owned, wrong slot), the launcher answers with a `cosmetics` message whose `self` is the stored set, which reverts the local change.

id.description: The item id, or null to empty the slot.

msg_cosmetics.title: cosmetics (Rust to Java)
msg_cosmetics.description: Equipped cosmetics. `self` is the local player's own set, sent after every `hello` and after any change (an equip from the launcher Store, a refused in-game equip, a purchase); null when the player has no online session (offline account, backend unreachable or not configured). `players` is a delta: other VOID players' sets that are new or changed since the last message, in reply to `cosmetics_query`; never a full roster, the mod keeps its own cache. Assets are bundled in the mod jar under `assets/void/cosmetics/<id>/`, so an id is all the mod needs; an id it does not have is skipped.

self.description: The local player's equipped set, or null with no online session.

players.description: Other VOID players' sets, new or changed.

msg_emote_remote.title: emote (Rust to Java)
msg_emote_remote.description: Another VOID player on the same server played an emote. Relayed from the server's Realtime channel; the sender's identity was stamped by the backend, not claimed by the sender. The mod plays it on that player if it can see them and drops it otherwise.

at.description: When it was played, Unix milliseconds on the backend's clock, so the mod can drop one that arrives stale.

mc_uuid.title: Minecraft UUID
mc_uuid.description: A Minecraft profile UUID. Rust always sends the dashed lowercase form and accepts the undashed form from the mod.

cosmetic_id.title: Cosmetic item id
cosmetic_id.description: Kebab-case, globally unique, e.g. `void-cape-rift`. Defined in `cosmetics.json`.

cosmetic_slot.title: Cosmetic slot
cosmetic_slot.description: A wearable slot, one item each. `back` is wings and other back items, `head` hats, `face` masks, `halo` floats above the head and may coexist with a hat, `trail` particles while moving, `badge` the icon beside the nametag. Emotes are not a slot.

equipped_set.title: Equipped set
equipped_set.description: What one player wears. Every slot is present, null when empty. `emotes` is the player's wheel, at most 8, in wheel order. `tints` is an optional per-slot recolour for items flagged `tintable`, omitted when empty.

emotes.description: Emote ids on the wheel, in order.

tints.description: Slot name to `#rrggbb` recolour, for tintable items only.

global_settings.title: Global settings
global_settings.description: The subset of §8.3 global settings the game needs. Account, Java path and RAM stay on the Rust side and are deliberately absent: they are launcher concerns and the mod has no use for them. additionalProperties is true so the launcher can add a global without a protocol bump.

menu_key.description: Key that opens and closes VoidMenuScreen. Right Shift by default (§6.3).

cycle_loadout_key.description: Key that cycles to the next loadout in the library. L by default (§6.3).

theme.description: Name of the design-token theme both renderers use.

ui_scale.description: Extra multiplier on the in-game UI, applied on top of MC GUI scale x window DPI (§6.2). 1 means follow the game.

hud_editor_grid.description: Snap grid size in unscaled GUI pixels used by the HUD editor. 0 disables snapping.
